recommendation: Keep the source fix. It resolves a parallel-page inconsistency without duplicating already-published related issue commits. If the work group later wants stricter rules about documenting per-query parameter support only in OperationDefinition, that should be handled as a separate follow-up because FHIR-31491 and the current Search page allow text or constrained OperationDefinition documentation.
issue_request: FHIR-31491 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5. It asked to clarify that named-query standard search parameters are potentially available, that resource-specific parameters are potentially available when the query operation has a resource scope, that servers need not support inherited parameters unless documented, that clients should rely on general-search CapabilityStatement support, and that authors should enumerate relevant named-query parameters where possible.
initial_application: Git commit ddecc63591d23dab5767aa2888c985a7c75964b6 applied the requested clarification to source/search.html. The current active Search page still carries that language at source/search.html:4789-4809, but the later OperationDefinition notes paragraph used older divergent wording.
additional_context: source/search.html is active via publish.ini and source/hierarchy.xml, and OperationDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini. Later related issues FHIR-39318 and FHIR-39316 are already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-39318 explains why OperationDefinition has parallel named-query prose, while FHIR-39316 supports the Patient-scoped parameter examples. FHIR-I minutes corroborate the FHIR-31491 disposition, and no direct Zulip discussion for FHIR-31491 was found.
reconciliation: Updated source/operationdefinition/operationdefinition-notes.xml to link to the Search named-query guidance, use potentially-available terminology, clarify resource-type-context parameter availability, distinguish definition from server support, point clients to CapabilityStatement support for general searches, and recommend documenting relevant parameters in OperationDefinition or a constrained OperationDefinition.
